hypotheses.statement: For mechanically wounded seven-week-old Arabidopsis thaliana, independently calibrated PMT and EMCCD measurements of the 400–870 nm photon-emission-rate-density integral over the first 30 minutes after incision will be equivalent within ±15%.

scope.population: Seven-week-old Arabidopsis thaliana plants, with at least 30 plants per detector comparison
scope.condition: Two-hour dark adaptation followed by a standardized sharp leaf incision and simultaneous 30-minute acquisition
scope.comparator: A red-sensitive photon-counting PMT versus a back-illuminated EMCCD viewing the same leaf through a calibrated beam splitter
scope.outcome: Background-subtracted 400–870 nm photon emission per second per square centimetre, integrated over 30 minutes

hypotheses.null_hypothesis: The 90% confidence interval for the PMT-to-EMCCD mean emission-density ratio is not wholly contained within 0.85–1.15.
hypotheses.estimand: Ratio of geometric-mean calibrated 30-minute emission-density integrals from the PMT and EMCCD.

rationale.step: The seed brief identifies the absence of absolute photon units and direct instrument comparability as the metrology hole.
Standardized incision of seven-week-old Arabidopsis produces measurable UPE extending through 400–870 nm, with a dominant 700–750 nm contribution.

A prior wound-emission experiment could not accurately analyze 700–720 nm because of its PMT photocathode sensitivity, demonstrating that detector response can limit comparability in the relevant band.

For each wavelength bin, emission-rate density is computed as Jλ=(Cλ-Dλ)/(t·A·Gλ·QEλ·Tλ), where Cλ is sample counts, Dλ is matched dark counts, t is acquisition time, A is emitting area, Gλ is calibrated collection efficiency, QEλ is detector efficiency, and Tλ is optical transmission.

hypotheses.proposed_experiment: Calibrate both detector paths with the same wavelength-scanned low-flux transfer source, measure beam-splitter ratio and collection geometry, then acquire injured leaves and shuttered dark frames simultaneously. Convert both count streams to photon s^-1 cm^-2 and perform a preregistered paired equivalence test with bounds 0.85–1.15.
hypotheses.required_instrument: Thermoelectrically cooled red-sensitive photon-counting PMT and back-illuminated EMCCD, both characterized from 400 to 870 nm, plus a calibrated beam splitter and tunable low-flux source.
hypotheses.novelty_self_claim: This tests whether a complete calibration chain makes two detector classes agree on absolute wound-induced UPE, rather than advancing another biological stress association already covered by the register.

hypotheses.statement: For wounded Arabidopsis thaliana leaves, replacing wavelength-resolved response correction with a single quantum-efficiency value specified at 500 nm will bias the inferred 400–870 nm photon-emission-rate density by at least 25%.

scope.population: Mechanically wounded seven-week-old Arabidopsis thaliana leaves
scope.condition: First 30 minutes after standardized incision following two-hour dark adaptation
scope.comparator: A scalar correction using QE at 500 nm versus correction using measured QE and optical transmission in wavelength bins across 400–870 nm
scope.outcome: Relative error in total photon-emission-rate density and in the estimated 700–870 nm emission fraction

hypotheses.null_hypothesis: The absolute relative difference between scalar-QE and wavelength-resolved estimates is less than 25%.

rationale.step: Wound-induced Arabidopsis emission is spectrally nonuniform and is dominated by 700–750 nm, with additional emission reported from 750–870 nm.
Plant lipid-peroxidation UPE has independently been reported to peak near 680 nm, while another wound study explicitly reported inadequate PMT sensitivity near 700–720 nm.
A human UPE spectrometer study identified wavelength-dependent spectrograph transmission and dark signal as constraints on spectral measurement.
The scalar estimate is Jscalar=Σλ(Cλ-Dλ)/(QE500·T500), whereas the spectral estimate is Jspectral=Σλ(Cλ-Dλ)/(QEλ·Tλ); their relative difference directly quantifies spectral-mismatch bias.

hypotheses.proposed_experiment: Record injured-leaf emission with a calibrated imaging spectrograph or contiguous bandpass filters, determine end-to-end response at each wavelength using a low-flux source, and process the identical raw observations with scalar and wavelength-resolved corrections.
hypotheses.required_instrument: Back-illuminated cooled EMCCD spectrograph or red-enhanced photon-counting PMT with contiguous bandpass filters, covering 400–870 nm.
hypotheses.novelty_self_claim: This exposes the hidden assumption that one quoted QE can convert broadband counts into photons despite strongly red-weighted biological emission.

hypotheses.statement: After two hours of thermal equilibration, cooled PMT dark counts collected over 48 hours will be Poisson-compatible enough that every six-hour block has a Fano factor of 0.8–1.2 and its empirical one-sided 95% blank threshold is no more than 10% above the Poisson-derived threshold.

scope.population: At least three low-dark-count PMT models tested in three light-tight UPE chambers
scope.condition: Fixed gain and detector temperature, two-hour equilibration, followed by continuous 48-hour shuttered acquisition in 60-second bins
scope.comparator: Empirical block-specific blank distribution versus a stationary Poisson model with the same mean
scope.outcome: Fano factor and the ratio of empirical to Poisson one-sided 95% thresholds, also expressed as photon s^-1 cm^-2 after calibration

hypotheses.null_hypothesis: At least one detector has a six-hour block with Fano factor outside 0.8–1.2 or an empirical 95% threshold more than 10% above the Poisson threshold.
hypotheses.estimand: For each detector and block, F=Var(C)/Mean(C) and RLOD=Q0.95,empirical/Q0.95,Poisson.

rationale.step: Dark-count measurements without germinating seeds have been reported to show ordinary rather than anomalous temporal scaling.
Basal and several wound-experiment photocount states have been reported to approximate Poisson distributions.
The UPE review notes that detector dark counts are central to instrument choice and that signal-to-noise ratio of at least one is commonly required.

Fano factor tests dispersion independently of count scale, while the empirical-to-Poisson threshold ratio measures how much a stationary-Poisson assumption understates the blank-defined detection threshold.

hypotheses.proposed_experiment: Distribute an identical acquisition protocol to three laboratories, log detector and chamber temperatures, acquire continuous shuttered counts, and analyze preregistered six-hour blocks without removing bursts except under explicit hardware-fault rules. Convert thresholds using each detector's wavelength-dependent efficiency and collection geometry.
hypotheses.required_instrument: Thermoelectrically cooled photon-counting PMTs sensitive over approximately 300–800 nm, with electronic shutters, temperature logging, and traceable low-flux efficiency calibration.
hypotheses.novelty_self_claim: This directly tests the stationary-Poisson dark-noise assumption on which many count-subtraction and LOD calculations implicitly depend.

hypotheses.statement: Centrally prepared sealed ampoules containing 100 mmol/L hydrogen peroxide in ultrapure water will provide a transferable ultraweak-luminescence reference whose 350–800 nm emission-rate density has within-laboratory ampoule CV no greater than 10% and between-laboratory bias no greater than 15% during minutes 5–15 at 25 °C.

scope.population: A single centrally prepared lot of sealed quartz ampoules containing 100 mmol/L hydrogen peroxide in ultrapure water
scope.condition: Measurement at 25 °C during a fixed 5–15 minute window after placement in the optical cavity
scope.comparator: Replicate ampoules within each laboratory and consensus emission-rate density across at least three laboratories
scope.outcome: Absolute 350–800 nm photon emission per second per cubic centimetre

hypotheses.null_hypothesis: Within-laboratory ampoule CV exceeds 10% in any laboratory or at least one laboratory's mean differs from the cross-laboratory consensus by more than 15%.
hypotheses.estimand: Maximum within-laboratory coefficient of variation and maximum absolute laboratory deviation from the consensus mean.

rationale.step: Non-catalytic hydrogen-peroxide disproportionation in pure water has been detected as ultraweak luminescence using a high-albedo quartz-powder Ulbricht cavity and photon counter.

The same work reports conversion of an extended isotropic photon source into a smaller Lambertian output with approximately 50% number efficiency and reports a detection limit in photon-emission-rate-density units.
The seed brief identifies reference materials and an inter-laboratory comparison as missing components of the UPE calibration chain.
Within-laboratory CV is SD(J)/Mean(J), and laboratory bias is |Mean(Jlab)-Mean(Jconsensus)|/Mean(Jconsensus); the stated bounds therefore give unambiguous acceptance criteria.

hypotheses.proposed_experiment: Prepare, randomize, and blind-code one ampoule lot; distribute it with identical quartz-powder cavities and a spectral calibration protocol to three laboratories; acquire matched water blanks and replicate ampoules; and compare absolute volume-normalized emission without laboratory-specific rescaling.
hypotheses.required_instrument: High-albedo quartz-powder Ulbricht cavity coupled to a calibrated cooled silicon single-photon counter or low-dark-count PMT covering 350–800 nm.
hypotheses.novelty_self_claim: This proposes and quantitatively qualifies a matrix-matched transfer reference for UPE-level emission, addressing the reference-material gap rather than another biological mechanism.

hypotheses.statement: For matched astrocyte and glioblastoma cultures containing 10^6 viable cells per well, at least 90% of replicate wells in each cell class will produce a calibrated 350–800 nm emission-rate density whose lower 95% confidence bound exceeds the empirical blank-defined LOD.

scope.population: Cultured astrocytes and glioblastoma cells normalized to 10^6 viable cells per well, with at least 30 wells per class
scope.condition: Fixed medium volume, temperature and dark-adaptation interval, followed by a 30-minute spontaneous-emission measurement
scope.comparator: Cell-free medium wells handled identically and interleaved throughout acquisition
scope.outcome: Fraction of cell-containing wells exceeding an empirical absolute LOD in photon s^-1 cm^-2

hypotheses.null_hypothesis: Fewer than 90% of wells in either cell class have a lower 95% confidence bound above the blank-defined LOD.
hypotheses.estimand: Detection probability in each cell class and the median ratio of net emission-rate density to absolute LOD.

rationale.step: Initial astrocyte and glioblastoma measurements reported clear separation of cellular signals from dark noise using ultra-sensitive photon-counting setups.
That study identifies further optical integration and detector cooling as setup optimizations, indicating that detection performance remains instrument-dependent.
Absolute photon-emission-rate-density LOD is required for direct sensitivity comparison, but is rarely reported in luminescence detection studies.
For each well, the decision statistic is S=(Jcell-Jblank)/LOD; detection requires the lower 95% confidence bound of S to exceed one.

hypotheses.proposed_experiment: Randomize cell and medium-only wells, interleave shuttered and medium blanks, calibrate end-to-end efficiency and collection geometry, and report both net emission density and a blank-distribution LOD. Repeat the campaign with a PMT and a silicon photon counter.
hypotheses.required_instrument: Low-dark-count cooled PMT and independently calibrated silicon single-photon counter with quartz collection optics covering 350–800 nm.
hypotheses.novelty_self_claim: This converts a reported qualitative separation from dark noise into a preregistered absolute-unit detection claim that another laboratory can directly reproduce.

hypotheses.statement: A malignancy classifier trained in one laboratory on calibrated 400–800 nm UPE emission-rate-density time series from a 13-cell-line malignant/non-malignant panel will achieve AUROC of at least 0.80 without model refitting in each of two laboratories using different detector classes.

scope.population: The 13 human and mouse malignant and non-malignant cell-line panel represented by 10^6 viable cells per plate
scope.condition: Standardized culture, medium, dark adaptation and 100-second acquisition protocol at three laboratories
scope.comparator: External laboratories using detector classes different from the training laboratory, with predictions from the frozen training-laboratory model
scope.outcome: Held-out laboratory AUROC for malignant versus non-malignant classification using absolute time-series and temporal power-density features

hypotheses.null_hypothesis: The frozen classifier has AUROC below 0.80 in either external laboratory.
hypotheses.estimand: Minimum AUROC across the two external laboratories, with cell line rather than plate used as the resampling unit.

rationale.step: A 13-cell-line in vitro study reported increased emission from tumor cells and 90% discrimination using temporal spectral-power-density features derived from 100-second photon measurements.
The UPE literature explicitly characterizes the absence of standardization as preventing UPE from becoming a reliable biomarker.
Lack of absolute photon and emission-density LOD reporting precludes direct sensitivity comparison between luminescence instruments.
Each raw bin is transformed to J(t)=[C(t)-D(t)]/[A·G·QEeff·Δt], after which the frozen feature transformation and classifier are applied identically at every laboratory.
The hypothesis is accepted only if both external AUROCs are at least 0.80; taking their minimum prevents a high-performing laboratory from masking a portability failure.

hypotheses.proposed_experiment: Distribute authenticated cell stocks and a locked acquisition protocol to three laboratories using, respectively, a PMT, EMCCD and silicon photon counter. Calibrate wavelength response, geometry, dark distribution and LOD locally; train once at the designated laboratory; freeze preprocessing and model coefficients; and evaluate blinded external plates without threshold adjustment.
hypotheses.required_instrument: Calibrated photon-counting PMT, back-illuminated EMCCD, or cooled silicon single-photon detector with characterized response across 400–800 nm.
hypotheses.novelty_self_claim: This tests whether absolute calibration makes a published cell-state signal transportable across laboratories and detector classes, rather than merely reproducing within-instrument discrimination.
